details.analysis:
TL;DR: Nvidia’s absolute R&D outlays have ramped sharply since 2021 and moved above the peer average in 2022–24, signaling aggressive product development to support large customer deployments. The calendar-series shows a peak in 2024 then a lower 2025 tally in the extract, which likely reflects timing shifts in reporting rather than a pullback in product-driven investment.

Key points:
- SQL numbers: NVDA calendar R&D — 2020: $8.07B; 2021: $11.28B; 2022: $15.72B; 2023: $19.34B; 2024: $26.40B; 2025: $16.90B vs peer averages of $12.66B, $14.09B, $16.73B, $17.07B, $19.49B, $6.79B respectively.
- Adoption signal — absolute spend surge (2022→2024) aligns with product ramps (AI datacenter GPUs, software stack) and implies NVDA is investing to scale capacity, features, and integration that customers demand.
- Customer traction proxy — NVDA moving from below to above peer average in absolute R&D while simultaneously growing revenues (impacting R&D % patterns) typically indicates demand-driven reinvestment rather than discretionary cost increases.
- Timing nuance: the drop in the 2025 calendar aggregate vs. 2024 likely reflects fiscal vs calendar aggregation, lumpy quarter timing, or one‑time items; persistent high historical levels still point to sustained engineering prioritization.

(Watchouts: reconcile calendar vs fiscal/LTM reporting and confirm revenue/product ramp timing before inferring a structural cut or shift in customer demand.)
